title: Sherlock Holmes: A Study in Scarlet — Ep 04/14 — "What John Rance Had to Tell"
description:
A Study in Scarlet, Episode 4. Holmes has read a man's height off the length of his stride, and his age off the width of a puddle, and Watson has heard enough certainty for one morning.

Told in Watson's own voice, cut to under three minutes. They drive out to Audley Court, where the washing hangs across the air and the children play on the flags, to hear the constable who found the body. John Rance has a story and no wish to tell it, until a half-sovereign turns over between Holmes's finger and thumb. What he then describes — a lamp burning at two in the morning, a light in an empty house, and a drunk man leaning on the railings, muffled to the eyes — is the one thing in the case that Holmes wanted, and Rance had it in his hands and let it walk away.

SOURCE
"A Study in Scarlet" by Arthur Conan Doyle, first published 1887. This episode adapts Chapter IV, "What John Rance Had to Tell". The book is in the public domain. Full text from Project Gutenberg: https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/244

HOW THIS WAS MADE
Every picture and every voice in this video is generated with AI. The words are adapted from Arthur Conan Doyle's text and edited by a person; the narration is a synthetic voice, not a recording of anyone; no shot is footage of a real person, a real place or a real event. This video is also declared as altered or synthetic content in YouTube's own disclosure field.
